questions.answer: No; confidence is the strength of belief.
questions.feedback: Check the definition and explain it in your own words before retrying.

questions.prompt: With prior odds 1:4 and likelihood ratio 2, what are posterior odds?
questions.feedback: Check the distinction or calculation against the worked case; correct the first unsupported step.

questions.prompt: Why distinguish confidence from an action threshold?
questions.answer: The costs and constraints of action may require a different threshold from an evidential judgement.
questions.feedback: State a concrete implication or limitation and retry without notes.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only.
scoring.practice: Updates confidence transparently, handles dependence and separates belief from action.
scoring.transfer: Submit a final epistemic audit containing a claim map, testimony chain, theory comparison and confidence update. Include one case where suspending judgement is warranted and one where action is justified despite residual uncertainty.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; quiz score alone is insufficient.
